cues.en: Another way to do collaborative filtering is by flipping the problem on its head.
cues.zh: 協同過濾的另一種做法，是把問題反過來。

cues.en: Instead of looking for other people similar to you and recommending stuff they liked, look at the things you liked and recommend stuff that's similar to those things.
cues.zh: 不找與你相似的人、推薦他們喜歡的東西，而是看你喜歡的項目，再推薦相似項目。

cues.en: We call this item-based collaborative filtering instead of user-based.
cues.zh: 這叫做項目式協同過濾，而不是使用者式。

cues.en: There are a few reasons why using similarities between items could be better than similarities between people.
cues.zh: 使用項目間相似度，可能比使用人與人之間的相似度更好，有幾個原因。

cues.en: One is that items tend to be of a more permanent nature than people.
cues.zh: 一個原因是，項目通常比人更固定。

cues.en: A math book will always be a math book.
cues.zh: 數學書永遠是數學書。

cues.en: But an individual's tastes may change very quickly over the span of their lives.
cues.zh: 但人的品味，在一生中可能很快改變。

cues.en: So focusing on the similarities between unchanging objects can produce better results than looking at similarities between people who may have liked something last week and something totally different this week.
cues.zh: 因此，專注於不變物件的相似度，可能比觀察上週喜歡某件事、本週又喜歡完全不同東西的人的相似度，產生更好結果。

cues.en: Your math book will always be similar to other math books, but a person who liked a math book might be bored with math a few months from now.
cues.zh: 數學書永遠與其他數學書相似，但喜歡數學書的人，幾個月後可能已對數學感到厭倦。

cues.en: And such, you can get away with computing an item similarity matrix less often than user similarities, because it won't change very quickly.
cues.zh: 因此，項目相似度矩陣不必像使用者相似度那麼頻繁計算，因為不會快速改變。

cues.en: Another very important advantage to building item similarities, is that you usually have far fewer items to deal with than people.
cues.zh: 建立項目相似度的另一個重要優點，是通常項目數量遠少於人數。

cues.en: Whatever company you're developing a Recommender System for, probably has a relatively small product catalog compared to the number of customers they have.
cues.zh: 無論替哪家公司開發推薦系統，它的商品目錄，與顧客數相比，可能都相對小。

cues.en: There are way more people than there are things to recommend to them in most cases.
cues.zh: 大多數情況，人數遠多於可推薦的項目數。

cues.en: This means that a 2D Matrix Mapping Similarity Score is between every item in your catalog, will be much smaller than a 2D Matrix mapping similarities between every user that visits your site.
cues.zh: 這表示，記錄目錄中每對項目相似度的二維矩陣，會比記錄網站每對訪客相似度的矩陣小得多。

cues.en: Not only does that make it simpler to store that matrix, it makes it faster to compute, as well.
cues.zh: 不只更容易儲存，計算也更快。

cues.en: And when you're dealing with massive systems like Amazon or Netflix, computational efficiency is very important.
cues.zh: 處理 Amazon 或 Netflix 這種大型系統時，運算效率非常重要。

cues.en: Not only does it require a fewer resources, it means you can you regenerate your similarities between items more often, making your system more responsive when new items are introduced.
cues.zh: 不只需要較少資源，也能更頻繁地重新產生項目相似度，讓新項目加入時，系統更快反應。

cues.en: Using item similarities also makes for a better experience for new users.
cues.zh: 使用項目相似度，對新使用者的體驗也更好。

cues.en: When a new user comes to your website, as soon as they have indicated interest in one thing, you can recommend items similar to that thing to them.
cues.zh: 新使用者來到網站，只要對一個項目表示興趣，就能推薦與那個項目相似的其他項目。

cues.en: With user-based collaborative filtering, you wouldn't have any recommendations for a new user at all until they make it into the next build of your use a similarity matrix.
cues.zh: 若使用使用者式協同過濾，則必須等新使用者納入下一次建立的使用者相似度矩陣，才能產生任何推薦。

cues.en: So the general process for item-based collaborative filtering is really the same as user-based.
cues.zh: 因此，項目式協同過濾的一般流程，與使用者式相同。

cues.en: The only difference is that we flip the use of users and items.
cues.zh: 唯一差別，是對調使用者與項目的角色。

cues.en: So instead of starting with a matrix that has users as rows and items as columns, we're starting with items as the rows and users as the columns.
cues.zh: 所以，不再從使用者為列、項目為欄的矩陣開始，而是以項目為列、使用者為欄。

cues.en: This let's us look up all the user ratings for a given item quickly, so we can measure similarity between items based on the users that rated them.
cues.zh: 這讓我們能快速查詢某個項目的所有使用者評分，再根據評分者，衡量項目之間的相似度。

cues.en: Before, we thought of users existing in a space where every item was a dimension, and found the cosine similarity between these user vectors.
cues.zh: 先前，把使用者想成存在於每個項目各為一個維度的空間，再計算使用者向量間的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: But now we're just flipping that.
cues.zh: 現在只是反過來。

cues.en: We're thinking of items existing in a space where every user is a dimension and finding the cosine similarity between these item vectors.
cues.zh: 把項目想成存在於每位使用者各為一個維度的空間，計算項目向量間的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: Of course, cosine similarity is just one of many ways to measure the similarity between items, and there may be other ways of scoring these item pairs that aren't based on similarity at all.
cues.zh: 當然，餘弦相似度只是衡量項目相似度的眾多方法之一，也可能有其他根本不以相似度為基礎的項目配對評分方法。

cues.en: But I can't get into that without violating NDAs.
cues.zh: 但談得更深入，就會違反保密協議。

cues.en: So now we can compute the cosine similarity scores between every possible item pair based on the users each item has in common who rated them.
cues.zh: 現在，可以根據每個項目的共同評分使用者，計算每對可能項目的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: Again, in this example, all of our scores come out to one or zero because we have so little data to work with.
cues.zh: 同樣地，這個例子資料太少，所以所有分數不是一就是零。

cues.en: But in the real world, you'd see more interesting and meaningful numbers here.
cues.zh: 真實世界中，會有更有意思、更有意義的數字。

cues.en: You might also notice that we ended up with a larger matrix than when we looked at user similarities.
cues.zh: 也可能注意到，最後的矩陣，比看使用者相似度時更大。

cues.en: But again, that's just a quirk of our example data.
cues.zh: 但同樣地，那只是範例資料的特殊情況。

cues.en: Normally you would have more users than items, not the other way around.
cues.zh: 通常，使用者比項目多，而不是相反。

cues.en: And that would mean that your item similarity matrix will be smaller than a user similarity matrix would be.
cues.zh: 這就表示，項目相似度矩陣會比使用者相似度矩陣小。

cues.en: So let's go back to our friend, Bob.
cues.zh: 回到我們的朋友 Bob。

cues.en: All we know about Bob is that he likes Star Wars.
cues.zh: 關於 Bob，只知道他喜歡《星際大戰》。

cues.en: Maybe he's a new user, and that's the only thing we know about him so far.
cues.zh: 也許他是新使用者，目前只知道這一點。

cues.en: We can now consult our item-to-item similarity matrix to look up other movies similar to Star Wars based on the ratings of other users who watched Star Wars in the past.
cues.zh: 現在，可以查詢項目間相似度矩陣，根據其他看過《星際大戰》的使用者評分，找出與它相似的電影。

cues.en: Interestingly, this technique not only picks up The Empire Strikes Back, but also picks up Indiana Jones and The Incredibles, because Ann liked those too.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，這種方法不只找出《帝國大反擊》，也找出《印第安納瓊斯》與《超人特攻隊》，因為 Ann 也喜歡那些。

cues.en: So even in this tiny example data set, we're getting more interesting results from item-based collaborative filtering than we did with user-based collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 因此，即使在這麼小的範例資料集中，項目式協同過濾，也比使用者式產生更有意思的結果。
